examples.title: Transportation
examples.summary: Dantzig's cannery problem: ship cases from two plants to three markets at least freight cost. The demand rows' duals are the marginal delivery costs.

examples.title: Gas production
examples.summary: The tutorial's first project: enums, a .dat file and a .prj with hide_zero. Choose production levels within component stocks to maximise profit.

examples.title: Product planning
examples.summary: Inside or outside production with structs and display statements.

examples.title: Warehouse location
examples.summary: IBM's facility-location sample: open warehouses and assign each store to an open one, trading fixed costs against supply costs.

examples.title: Crew covering
examples.summary: Set covering for airline crews: pick the cheapest crews so that every flight is covered.

examples.title: Knapsack
examples.summary: A multi-resource integer knapsack, solved by branch and bound.

examples.title: Portfolio
examples.summary: Markowitz: the minimum-variance mix of five assets that reaches a target expected return. A convex QP.

examples.title: Pooling (non-convex)
examples.summary: Haverly's pooling problem: bilinear quality constraints make it non-convex; spatial branch and bound proves the global optimum of 400.

examples.title: N queens
examples.summary: Twelve queens on a 12 × 12 board, none attacking another, with three allDifferent constraints.

examples.title: SEND + MORE = MONEY
examples.summary: The classic cryptarithm: a different digit for each letter.

examples.title: Sudoku
examples.summary: Rows, columns and boxes as allDifferent constraints; propagation does most of the work.

examples.title: Job shop ft06
examples.summary: Fisher and Thompson's 6 × 6 benchmark with CP Optimizer interval variables and noOverlap. The proven optimum is a makespan of 55.

examples.title: Setup times
examples.summary: A sequence variable with job families: noOverlap with a setup-time matrix, and the setup cost through typeOfNext.

examples.title: Work calendar
examples.summary: Interval intensity from a step function: tasks stop over weekends, and inspections may not touch one (forbidExtent).

examples.title: House building
examples.summary: OPL 3 activities on three workers chosen by AlternativeResources; minimise the longest time a worker is on site.

examples.title: Efficient frontier
examples.summary: A main block in IBM ILOG Script that builds and solves one QP per target return.

examples.title: Solution pool
examples.summary: cplex.populate() keeps the optimum and enumerates every other feasible basket.
